learningGoals: Understand that describing words tell us more about naming words (nouns) in a fun way. 🧠
Identify and use color words (red, blue, yellow) to describe everyday objects. 🎨
Describe things based on their size (big, small, tall) and shape (round, square). 📏
Express feelings and qualities using simple describing words like happy, hot, or soft. 🥰
teachingTips: Ask descriptive questions daily: During routines, ask questions like 'What color is your shirt?' or 'Is your milk hot or cold?' 🗣️
Play 'I Spy' with adjectives: Say 'I spy with my little eye, something big and blue' to help them connect describing words to real objects. 🕵️‍♂️
Encourage detailed sentences: When they say 'Look at the car!', gently prompt them by asking, 'Wow! Is it a fast car or a slow car? What color is it?' 🚗
Use the sense of touch: Let them touch different items (a soft pillow, a hard block) and ask them to describe how it feels in their hands. 🖐️

funActivities.title: The Mystery Bag Game 🛍️
funActivities.description: Place a few familiar objects in an opaque bag. Ask your child to reach in, feel an object without looking, and use describing words (like soft, hard, round, or long) to guess what it is before pulling it out.

funActivities.title: Colorful Plate Hunt 🍽️
funActivities.description: During mealtime, ask your child to describe their food using colors, shapes, and tastes. For example, encourage them to say 'I am eating a red, sweet apple' or 'This is a round, warm chapati'.

funActivities.title: Nature Describing Walk 🚶‍♀️🌳
funActivities.description: Go for a short walk outside. Challenge your child to spot and describe 5 things using two describing words for each item, such as 'a tall green tree', 'a tiny black ant', or 'a fluffy white cloud'.
